ImmediateThread models a legal reader-completes-before-next-thread-start schedule. It is sufficient for observed double close, but does not model asynchronous scheduling, blocking ReadFile or join cancellation. Add deterministic scheduled fake threads, never real pipes/threads for this phase.

Set equality in existing pipe/duplicate tests catches leaks but not double close. A per-handle ledger must track kind, creation, transfer, inheritance, assignment, close attempts/outcomes and termination/wait state; assert exactly one owner on all intermediate steps.

Existing query/wait tests deliberately catch OSError then examine closes; record raised exception and structured-return absence explicitly. New cleanup tests should ensure one failure does not skip all later cleanup, not just assert a close was attempted.

Zero-highwater test removes kernel and ownership along with zero residency, demonstrating architectural insufficiency but not isolating each guard. Split into independent highwater-only, ownership-only, completed-kernel-only and multi/four-success-only cases.
